drafted_from: tool:keep-journey-steps-from-kept-rows's own row (its words, input schema and steps) and the journey kit's mapping file (read-data/journey-kept-rows.json)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep the journey steps of my pursuit from its bookings and paid sales", with {"credential_name":"ethos_for_who_runs_it-connection"}. It runs tool:keep-journey-steps-from-kept-rows and answers how many bookings and sales it read and newly kept.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads the statements and payment_events rows of the database named by credential_name and writes the journey_steps table, which the journey kit makes.
instructions: 1. Apply read-data/journey-steps.sql to the pursuit's database once (tool:run-sql-in-my-database), so journey_steps exists.
2. Say to your AI: "Keep the journey steps of my pursuit from its bookings and paid sales", and give it credential_name, the held name of the database connection string.
3. Read the answer: each mapping in read-data/journey-kept-rows.json shows how many rows it read and how many steps it newly kept. Running it again keeps nothing new.

worked_examples.title: Keep a pursuit's bookings and sales as journey steps
worked_examples.ask: Keep the journey steps of my pursuit from its bookings and paid sales
worked_examples.hands_back: It answers { mappings: [{ id: "tidycal-bookings-from-statements", step: "booking", read: n, kept: k }, { id: "stripe-sales-from-payment-events", step: "sale", read: n, kept: k }] }, with kept at 0 on a second run.
